I think these can still be in GpuSensor

GpuSensor represents a Gpu Temperature Sensor. We want to create all different type of sensors per device. createSensors will create all the sensors for a device. The read function will update all the sensors of a device. Renamed createSensors to makeSensors to avoid confusion with free function createSensors.
Can still be in GpuSensor
GpuSensor represents a Gpu Temperature Sensor, and since this functions is related to the device it is put in GpuDevice.
Do we really need this though for this/immedeately following commit. If this is about multi-GPU support, then we don't need to bring that in now in this commit.
Even for single GPU support we need a map from name to the device object, since we want to remove it on interface removed signals.

Isn't what we need to pass to createSensors just an EID? I was thinking if this could be something like:

eids = discoverGpus(...) // MCTP discovery, EM processing, Query Devices
createSensors(..., eid) // Read and Update sensor values, as before
I think discoverGpus would also return a list of sensorIDs (eventually we could also get those from EM).
Since we are using async io with callbacks these functions just cannot simply return the results. createSensors is name referenced from ipmb, we can rename it to discoverGpus if it sounds confusing.
Acknowledged
This abstraction doesn't really seem useful?
We need common interface to update the sensor, so that we can update them periodically. The class Sensor doesn't provide it. See GpuDevice::read which does polling of all the sensors of a device.
A lot of this was in `GpuTempSensor`. Why didn't we start with the `GpuDevice` abstraction rather than move it all now?

The earlier commits were aligned with: mplement basic temperature reading in C++ using a minimum implementation.

We didn't require the GpuDevice abstraction to read a single temperature sensor. It's required here to enable other sensors.

Separate files provide ease of reading and separation of logic without any cost. DeviceDiscoveryManager class manages state that is needed to query each MCTP endpoint. it is also created when the presence of the EM config is detected and it is also being removed when that EM config is removed. Having this common logic in one class provide more readability and the design pattern is same as observed in other dbus-sensors.
